about: Every outside source the tracker relies on, and every claim the public site makes or plans to make, with how it is backed. Status values. Sources: live-data (our code reads it directly), checked (opened and the specific fact confirmed, with date), cited (from docs/research, not re-opened for this use), rejected (tested or considered and not used). Claims: measured (our own test, see evidence), sourced (backed by a checked source), unverified (needs a source before it is published), to-confirm (Philip must confirm). Rule: add a source here the moment research uses it. Nothing marked unverified or to-confirm goes on the public site. This file is the full reading list. The public site's reference list is derived from it: a source is listed on the site only if a claim published on the site cites it, like a paper's references.

claims.text: Satellites saw N hectares of land cleared in the last 12 months (patches of at least 1 ha, confirmed loss of at least half the plant cover)
N% of it is land with no licence to mine
claims.caveat: Only as complete as the public cadastre

claims.text: 104 of 117 randomly checked patches showed signs of mining
claims.where: home ("mostly large ones, small new patches are more often farms"), /method
claims.caveat: Judged by Claude from pictures, mostly large patches. For small patches first seen in the last six months only 8 to 11 of 20 showed mining (s22), so the share must say which patches it covers. Philip's one-time check and an area-weighted, season-aware random check across all tiles are still to do before launch

claims.text: Hectares cleared in the 12 months before each monthly point, measured on the same day each month, compared with a year before
NASA confirms clearing weeks or months after first seeing it, and drops it from the data about a year later

claims.text: Status 6 and 8 mean confirmed loss of at least 50% of plant cover, ongoing or finished
A football pitch is 105 by 68 m, 0.714 ha; 1 ha is about 1.4 pitches
A published radar method flagged pixels of which only about 6% were mining
River colour changes more between pictures than between years
NASA's yearly product made clearing look as if it had halved
NASA's surface water data missed the mining ponds
claims.caveat: 'Smaller than its 30 m pixels' is our explanation, not a measurement
